statement: Let Z(s,D) = (D/pi)^s Gamma(s) zeta2(s,D) with zeta2(s,D) = (1/2) sum'_{j,k} (j^2 + D^2 k^2)^(-s) (analytic continuation). At D* = e^gamma/(4 pi): Z(1/2, D*) > 0, so D* is not a zero of zeta2(1/2, .) (refuting Conjecture 1.1 of Betermin-Samaj-Travenec, arXiv:2110.09368). Moreover Z(1/2, D* + 1e-20) < 0, so a zero lies in (D*, D* + 1e-20).

arb_ball_arithmetic.definition_based: Z(1/2,D) = -2 + int_1^T t^(-1/2) [theta3(e^{-pi t D}) theta3(e^{-pi t/D}) - 1] dt + tail, T = 600, Arb rigorous integral, tail bounded by 4.1 T^(-1/2) e^(-pi D T)/(pi D)

true_root.source: code/04-epstein-conjecture/epstein_check.py (mpmath, 70 digits; the definition and the Bessel series agree to about 70 digits at Delta*, 0.3 and 0.14 and about 40 digits at 0.9)

caveats: The Bessel-series identity is derived by Poisson summation in papers/04-epstein-conjecture/main.md section 3 and cross-checked against the definition by Arb balls; it is not formalised in Lean.
Uniqueness of the zero on (0,1] is Lemma 4.4 of the cited paper; the refutation does not need it.
